= Repository wiki editions — source check and implementation, 2026-10-15 =

This continues [the Wiki in a Jar deep dive](../wikiinajar-deep-dive.md),
[the historical image/DjVu patch](wikiinajar-image-support.md), and the
[Haiku vault implementation](../src/lib/vaultfile.ts). The new executable build
is in [tools/wiki-workspace](../tools/wiki-workspace/README.md).
Machine-readable bibliography: [research/wiki-workspace-sources.json](../research/wiki-workspace-sources.json).

Follow-up: [verified Drive backup and historical 0.8 rebuild](drive-backup-wiki-2026-10-15.md).
The committed baseline was backed up before continuation; the original 0.8
archive is now locally recovered and its patched installation has fresh HTTP
checks. The separate More 0.9.9, JavaCard, Ghidra/native and live-service limits
below remain unchanged.

**Evidence labels:** *source-read* means the named files were retrieved from a
pinned GitHub commit and inspected this turn; *local test* means code actually
ran here; *proposal/pending* means it did not. Repository documentation from
prior investigations is not presented as a new live check of its remote sources.

== 1. The six requested steps, without mixing incompatible runtimes ==

| Step | Delivered | Boundary / pending work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — `wiki.in.a.jar` | New self-contained Java 11+ executable JAR with the classic browser wiki as its landing page, real ACME/TJWS HTTP, bundled docs/DjVu and exact repository bytes | This is a new host for the HTML5 conversion, **not** Java source translated from every HTML/JS application and **not** the original 0.8 binary |
| 2 — `more.wiki.in.a.jar` | Repository library landing page, one page per eligible file, explicit references/backlinks, immutable revision chain, optimistic write preconditions, encrypted page/file exchange | New “repository edition 1,” **not** a claim to have recovered Jens Fauth's historical 0.9.9 source |
| 3 — JVM / OpenJDK / Temurin / Ghidra | Compiled and executed with recovered Temurin 21.0.12.1+1; real `javap` disassembly; Java 8 applet reader; optional Ghidra inspection command | No full headless Ghidra installation was run; no JVM-to-C++ or native-assembly equivalence claim |
| 4 — ACME + DjVu + vault + JavaCard | Actual `Acme.Serve.Serve`, local WASM DjVu decoder, content-addressed vault, Haiku-v1-compatible WebCrypto exchange, JavaCard digest-applet source and compiled read-only PC/SC client | No CAP conversion, JavaCard SDK type-check, simulator/card deployment, encrypted mounted filesystem or QEMU port |
| 5 — TiddlyWiki / Webxdc | Native TiddlyWiki **5.4.1**, importable tiddlers, self-contained HTML engine, `.xdc` package with bounded plain-text chat updates and conflict copies | HTML/XDC contain source previews, metadata and a DjVu demo, **not** the entire binary vault; real messenger/device sync remains a deployment check |
| 6 — cross-checks / bibliography / MediaWiki | Per-file provenance and SHA-256, resolved links/backlinks and unresolved links, extracted URL bibliography, existing browser JSON converter, schema-valid MediaWiki 0.11 XML | No remote wiki was changed. XML schema validation is not an actual MediaWiki server import; attachments, contacts and dialect-specific namespaces need migration review |

All three executable JARs share one server implementation and complete snapshot;
only their default landing pages differ. The separate `wiki-reader-applet.jar`
is an AWT **read-only source reader**, with same-origin access to that snapshot.
It is not the JavaCard applet and does not run a server inside a browser plug-in.

== 2. Historical versions and the ACME correction ==

The repository's original patch points at Wiki in a Jar 0.8, the
`astecenko/Wiki-in-a-Jar` mirror commit
`a56cfdfc8d343f60c915825a01af24577846cede`, and the Drive-backed distribution
that was recovered in an earlier turn. That patch remains separate and
unchanged. Its XRays/NanoHTTPD provenance is documented in the previous
[image investigation](wikiinajar-image-support.md), with the exact distinction
also recorded in [the Lantronix deep dive](lantronix-uclinux-deep-dive-2026-10-08.md).

The new server really compiles `Acme/Serve/Serve.java`, not a JDK HTTP server
renamed “ACME.” Source-read: TJWS commit
`33920d0e429d3271796b3fd2d838cd0a47208846`, whose header credits Jef Poskanzer
and Dmitriy Rogatkin, whose `Serve` constructor accepts `ARG_PORT` and
`ARG_BINDADDRESS`, and whose servlet registry accepts the new wiki handler.
[1](https://github.com/drogatkin/TJWS2/blob/33920d0e429d3271796b3fd2d838cd0a47208846/1.x/src/Acme/Serve/Serve.java)

The small base container requires the older Servlet API plus TJWS compatibility
classes. Here they are compiled from the **source** of Tomcat 4.1.40's servletapi
in a pinned third-party mirror. This is not an official Apache-release signature
verification. Source archive hashes, original source and license notices are
included in every executable JAR; no precompiled mirror JAR is trusted as the
build input. [2](https://github.com/xcf007/tomcat4/tree/dbed311153d1d97d7c92534d173c853130b08fb4/apache-tomcat-4.1.40-src/servletapi)

GitHub repository searches for `morewikiinajar in:name` and
`"more-wiki-in-a-jar" in:name` returned zero results on this date. That is a
**narrow negative result**, not proof the historical source no longer exists.
The earlier deep dive's SourceForge/Wayback references are useful leads but
were not re-fetched here. The release identity must stay distinct until source
or binaries are recovered, hashed and compared.

=== HTTP/storage boundaries implemented ===

- Bind to loopback by default; `--bind 0.0.0.0` is explicit. Preview routing uses
  same-origin relative URLs, never a browser request to a sandbox's localhost.
- No stock file/CGI servlet, arbitrary filesystem route, WAR deployment, proxy,
  remote-URL fetch or code execution endpoint is registered.
- Only an explicit packaged asset manifest is served. Private paths, invalid
  encoding, dot segments, backslashes and traversal are rejected.
- `/vault/<sha256>` always downloads source bytes as octet-stream attachments.
  `/media/<sha256>` only accepts allowlisted raster/DjVu entries; HTML/SVG never
  become active vault content at the server's origin.
- Server persistence is opt-in with a high-entropy bearer token. Page writes
  require the current ETag, cap their body size, reject malformed UTF-8 and
  preserve immutable parent-linked revisions. Stale saves return 409.
- Private encrypted envelopes require the token for reads as well as writes.
  The server has no vault passphrase and cannot decrypt them.
- The public repository catalog, pages and page revisions are **not encrypted**.
  Anyone who can reach the HTTP server can read them. This is a local tool, not
  a hardened multi-tenant service or an ACME/TJWS security audit.

== 3. “Everything has a page” and versioning ==

`catalog.mjs` enumerates tracked files plus non-ignored workspace additions for
explicitly registered local repositories. It does not crawl all of a user's
GitHub/GitLab repositories or fetch linked websites. Registration is repeatable:

```sh
npm run build:wiki-workspace
node tools/wiki-workspace/build.mjs --repo OtherProject=/absolute/local/checkout
```

Each included regular file has a stable page id, source path, repository id,
SHA-256, byte length, MIME classification, preview hash, explicit outgoing
references and backlinks. Binary files get a metadata page rather than being
pretended to be readable source. Duplicate byte strings share one vault blob.
The snapshot digest covers sorted repository/path/content-hash tuples; source
Git commit ids are recorded separately. **This is a working-tree snapshot and
wiki revision system, not an embedded copy of the complete Git commit graph.**

Each exclusion is named in the manifest: `.git`, relay/Arena caches, private
import/export areas, known credential filenames, encrypted personal vaults,
build outputs and symlinks. Some caches were historically tracked despite
`.gitignore`, so the publication filter applies even to tracked paths. It is a
filename/path policy, **not a secret scanner**. Review source contents, licenses
and the manifest before distributing a snapshot.

The library follows explicit Markdown links, HTML `href`/`src` values and relative
module imports. Resolved links and backlinks are concrete edges, not an AI
assertion that two topics corroborate one another. Unresolved paths stay visible.
Extracted bibliographic URLs are marked **not automatically verified**. The
curated research bibliography below distinguishes them from the sources actually
inspected this turn.

Page edits do not change repository files. Initial text is a bounded preview
(96 KiB, explicitly marked if truncated); exact source bytes remain in the JAR.
Subsequent wiki page revisions live under `--data`, survive restart and can be
restored as new revisions. Local browser drafts are separate from that server
history and should be exported for backup.

== 4. Vault, S.S.E., Base64url and the “Base65” question ==

The existing Workbench has **two** separate mechanisms: `BookVfs` stores
content-addressed attachment bytes in IndexedDB, while `vaultfile.ts` encrypts
JSON exchange files. Neither automatically exposes a mounted encrypted filesystem
to Java. This build reuses the content-addressing design and the exact exchange
wire format; it does not silently read a user's existing wallet database.

The compatible format is:

```text
haiku-vault-v1. + Base64(01 | salt[16] | iv[12] | AES-256-GCM ciphertext+tag)
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 120000 iterations, UTF-8 passphrase
```

Local tests exercised both directions between the existing Noble-based
`src/lib/vaultfile.ts` and the new browser WebCrypto implementation, including
non-ASCII passphrases. Wrong-password and tamper rejection are tested. A decrypted
wallet/seed payload is **not** automatically turned into public wiki pages.
The new wiki requires a separate nonempty passphrase and has no default password.

In this repository, S.S.E. is **Secret Space Encryptor**, as shown by
[`sse-webxdc/index.html`](../sse-webxdc/index.html), not an implemented
server-sent-events or searchable-symmetric-encryption system. Source-read of
its referenced Android fork's `Encryptor.java` shows version-3 paths using
Argon2id and EAX and output codecs including HybridBase62 and SSEBase64.
This is a different container/KDF/AEAD combination from Haiku vault v1.
[3](https://github.com/sdatar59/Paranoia_Works-Secret_Space_Encryptor_for_Android/blob/31a19a4c8a5ea8fb8bce6a2a1b6f5cc40cc8f2f3/MainApp/src/main/java/com/paranoiaworks/unicus/android/sse/utils/Encryptor.java)

The inspected `SSEBase64Encoder` has 64 data symbols, uses `)` and `]` instead
of `+` and `/`, and declares `.` as padding. Its `SSEBase64` byte-array decoder
adds missing padding. These are precise source facts; they do **not** make it
RFC-style Base64url or a newly specified Base65 format.
[4](https://github.com/sdatar59/Paranoia_Works-Secret_Space_Encryptor_for_Android/blob/31a19a4c8a5ea8fb8bce6a2a1b6f5cc40cc8f2f3/CryptoLibs/src/main/java/sse/org/bouncycastle/util/encoders/SSEBase64Encoder.java)
[5](https://github.com/sdatar59/Paranoia_Works-Secret_Space_Encryptor_for_Android/blob/31a19a4c8a5ea8fb8bce6a2a1b6f5cc40cc8f2f3/CryptoLibs/src/main/java/sse/org/bouncycastle/util/encoders/SSEBase64.java)

**Decision:** keep format compatibility explicit. The new helper implements
strict, canonical, unpadded Base64url for transport where needed; the Haiku
file stays ordinary Base64. Encoding is not encryption. “Base65” remains
unspecified: no matching format was found in the inspected code. If it denotes
another custom alphabet/framing scheme, obtain that specification and test
vectors before implementing it. No SSE ciphertext is relabelled as a Haiku file.
A future Argon2id envelope would need a new version and migration tests, not an
unannounced change to version 1.

== 5. OpenJDK, Temurin, applets, Ghidra, native code and WASM ==

The recovered split JDK archive was reassembled only after its SHA-256 matched
`.relay/jdk/jdk21.sha256`. `java -version` reported **Temurin 21.0.12.1+1-LTS**.
The executable server targets Java 11 bytecode; the historical reader and
upstream container target Java 8. Adoptium's own repository describes Temurin
as OpenJDK binary builds, not a separate applet architecture.
[6](https://github.com/adoptium/temurin-build/blob/2dd5226b8fbfc3d075a9d5a75a1a4f710f4e306c/README.md)

“JVM” is the execution model, “JDK” the development tools/runtime, and “JRE” a
runtime distribution. No particular “OpenJRE” project was identified by the
request; it is not silently treated as a fourth interoperable SDK. Use a
maintained runtime matching the build target and verify distribution provenance.

Modern browsers do not provide the old Java plug-in model. The OpenJDK commit
implementing JEP 504 removes the Applet API; its actual commit was inspected,
not inferred from a misspelled product name. The compatibility reader is
therefore deliberately isolated from the modern server entry point. It was
compiled, but not run in a legacy browser or appletviewer here.
[7](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/5cf672e7784b9a9a82f29977a072b162cc240fd1)

Ghidra source contains `JVM:BE:32:default`, with a `JVM.sla` processor and
compiler specification. That supports a meaningful static-inspection path for
class files. It does not establish a correct Java-to-C++ translator.
[8](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/blob/61f664ff30d9bd7d5501956751d46553728c5f6b/Ghidra/Processors/JVM/data/languages/JVM.ldefs)

The build **actually ran** `javap -c -p -s` and emits `WikiServer.javap.txt`.
`inspect-jvm.sh` also produces verbose output and, **only when GHIDRA_HOME is
supplied**, imports the class into headless Ghidra using the repository's existing
`GenericProgramReport.java`. No Ghidra run or native instruction listing is
claimed in this report. A `.c` suffix from a decompiler would denote C-like
pseudocode, not a validated C/C++ port preserving JVM exceptions, GC, reflection,
class loading, strings and concurrency.

A GitHub search also located **pmietlicki/openjvm-wasm**. Its pinned README
claims OpenJDK 17 Zero via Emscripten, a canvas AWT/Swing toolkit, same-origin
network proxy and WebSocket-to-TCP bridge. It documents secure-context and
COOP/COEP requirements, and source builds rather than a trivial JAR rename.
These are **upstream claims read from source**, not reproduced locally. Its
application-specific SSO/proxy and JAR transformation features are not imported
into the vault's trust boundary.
[9](https://github.com/pmietlicki/openjvm-wasm/blob/03ec1f7c21ca9880661911617bf12e02069d8462/README.md)

=== Recommended options, in order ===

1. **Executable Java host + existing browser clients:** implemented, smallest
   semantic change, inspectable dependency sources, no legacy browser plug-in.
2. **Native TiddlyWiki / Webxdc:** implemented for portable notes and source
   previews; keep large binaries in the host's vault rather than chat updates.
3. **Native/AOT host:** investigate a supported Java AOT toolchain with explicit
   resource/reflection configuration and rerun the same HTTP/crypto tests. Not
   implemented or benchmarked; do not promise that reflective TJWS is automatic.
4. **JVM-on-WASM:** research prototype only; test startup size, interpreter cost,
   memory, browser storage and proxy isolation before choosing it for this app.
5. **C++ rewrite:** a separate implementation project with protocol, renderer,
   cryptographic and persistence parity tests—not “compile Ghidra output.”

== 6. JavaCardOS, QEMU and qcow2 ==

JavaCardOS's `pyResMan` describes an APDU/resource-management tool with
pyScard/GlobalPlatform dependencies. This is evidence for an ISO-7816 host/card
workflow, not evidence that an ordinary Java servlet/JVM runs on a card.
[10](https://github.com/JavaCardOS/pyResMan/blob/9a518dfdca087335628e184212aaa44d35f470f2/README.md)

The prototype here targets **JavaCard Classic**, not every possible JavaCard
profile. `VaultDigestApplet.java` stores a 32-byte snapshot digest, validates an
installation-supplied PIN, reads short APDUs and transactionally updates the
anchor. The host-side `CardAnchorClient` compiles with standard PC/SC APIs and
only selects/reads the applet on explicit CLI invocation. The HTTP server does
not expose a raw APDU endpoint. The JavaCard source passed the existing JDK
**parse-only** checker; no CAP, SDK verification, simulator or card test occurred.
See [the APDU contract and pending tests](../tools/wiki-workspace/javacard/README.md).

The inspected QEMU qcow2 specification distinguishes encryption method values
and an explicit LUKS encryption-header pointer extension. A qcow2 image is a
virtual block-device container, not the browser's content-addressed vault or a
JavaCard filesystem. This build neither implements it nor claims encryption by
renaming an archive. A WASM emulator also does not provide a physical secure
element's tamper resistance.
[11](https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/d5b5083cb783c447001e862c2b525e59f48ad78c/docs/interop/qcow2.rst)

== 7. Native TiddlyWiki, Tiddlyhost API and Webxdc ==

The npm package is locked to **5.4.1**. This build invokes its real engine with
the official vanilla/snowwhite themes and browser-storage plugin. In this version,
the boot JSON deserializer requires string-valued fields; array-valued `tags`
caused the initial fixture to become one raw JSON tiddler. A browser smoke test
caught that defect. Exporting `tags` as a string fixed it, and a regression test
now pins the rule. This is a useful source-level check, not merely a screenshot
of a page styled to resemble TiddlyWiki.
[12](https://github.com/TiddlyWiki/TiddlyWiki5/tree/v5.4.1)

A full-repository browser test caught a second, scale-dependent defect: a
browser-storage filter starting with `all[tiddlers]` discarded the plugin's
change iterator and attempted to save the entire corpus on every event. Storage
quota alerts then triggered more saves. The filter now retains only changed
non-system notes and selected state tiddlers, excludes alert/popup tiddlers,
and has a regression test using the **actual** 5.4.1 filter engine. A real browser
confirmed that a local note survives reload without copying the source corpus
into localStorage. Native HTML/XDC source previews additionally default to
4 KiB per file for portability; `--tw-preview-bytes` is configurable. Larger
96 KiB previews remain in the JSON/XML exchange and the host library, while
exact bytes are still in the JAR vault.

Repository sources stay `text/plain`, including HTML/JS. The generated trusted
metadata view provides outgoing links, backlinks and bibliographic fields.
The Webxdc module rejects system/plugin tiddler updates, caps message size and
retains concurrent changes as separate conflict tiddlers. Local browser-storage
and explicit HTML/JSON exports are the persistence path; binary attachments are
not smuggled through a note update.

=== Tiddlyhost: source-verified endpoints ===

Inspected commit `d573a5964a0e0b226f36aecfdc8b6362f09a0f14`, controller and routes:
[13](https://github.com/tiddlyhost/tiddlyhost-com/blob/d573a5964a0e0b226f36aecfdc8b6362f09a0f14/rails/app/controllers/tiddlywiki_controller.rb)
[14](https://github.com/tiddlyhost/tiddlyhost-com/blob/d573a5964a0e0b226f36aecfdc8b6362f09a0f14/rails/config/routes.rb)

| Route on an individual site | Observed behavior in source |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /` / `HEAD /` / `OPTIONS /` | wiki delivery and ETag; optional DAV header advertises PUT saving |
| `GET /tiddlers.json` | visibility-checked export; supports `include_system=1`, `skinny=1`, `title`, `pretty=1` |
| `GET /text/:title.tid` | one visible tiddler in `.tid` format |
| `GET /download` | HTML download, subject to visibility and the site's download setting |
| `GET /info` | save capability; last-saved metadata only when saveable |
| `PUT /` | owner/session-gated **whole-wiki** save; supplied stale `If-Match` can produce 412, unless the site's override disables this check |
| `POST /` | upload-saver whole-wiki flow, not an anonymous tiddler CRUD API |

The controller applies permissive CORS headers to the JSON/TID read endpoints,
not a blanket anonymous write API. Tiddlyhost's whole-file save semantics must
not be confused with the new host's per-page revision API. No Tiddlyhost account,
site identifier or target was supplied, and its host is not reachable here;
there was **no live API request or upload**. A future importer should default
to public, non-system tiddlers, record the source ETag, reject executable fields,
and require an explicit target and user confirmation before any whole-wiki save.

== 8. MediaWiki, not an invented “Wikimedia JSON format” ==

The inspected `wikimedia/mediawiki` repository identifies MediaWiki as PHP wiki
software used by Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. Wikimedia is not a
single writable wiki endpoint. The conversion targets a **MediaWiki import
format**, not a claim that arbitrary repository data belongs on Wikipedia.
[15](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki/blob/4f6bde3101f3a445f01418b143e043e976b77e40/README.md)

The converter accepts the existing `wikiinajar-jar` JSON version 1, retains
saved revisions and text, skips deleted pages and maps every title into a safe
`Repository/…` main-namespace title. Known internal links are rewritten; the
report retains original-to-imported title mappings. Raw source files render
literally in `<pre>` rather than becoming wiki templates. Unicode byte counts,
XML escaping, revision ids, origin ids and SHA-1 fields are generated explicitly.

The actual **0.11 XSD** was fetched from the pinned repository. It requires a
revision `<origin>` element: validating the first fixture exposed that missing
field, which is now generated and tested. The schema's W3C XML namespace import
is resolved to a second pinned local fixture; validation does not need network
access. Full validation uses `validate-mediawiki.py` and optional Python lxml.
[16](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki/blob/4f6bde3101f3a445f01418b143e043e976b77e40/docs/export-0.11.xsd)
[17](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki/blob/4f6bde3101f3a445f01418b143e043e976b77e40/tests/phpunit/maintenance/xml.xsd)

Source-read API examples include revision content with `rvslots` and `rvprop`.
The import implementation checks `importupload` permission for XML uploads and
requires POST/write mode. No remote API was called and no credentials were
requested. Read-only research queries for a user-chosen MediaWiki would look
like this (not an executed request):

```text
/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&titles=Some_page&rvslots=main&rvprop=ids|timestamp|content&format=json&formatversion=2
```

An authenticated import/edit workflow additionally needs the target's permission,
authentication and token rules. Prefer a disposable local wiki and inspect the
conversion report before enabling any write integration.
[18](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki/blob/4f6bde3101f3a445f01418b143e043e976b77e40/includes/Api/ApiQueryRevisions.php)
[19](https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki/blob/4f6bde3101f3a445f01418b143e043e976b77e40/includes/Api/ApiImport.php)

== 9. GitLab and Internet Archive: explicitly pending ==

Only the allowed GitHub/npm/Python hosts are reachable in this sandbox. GitLab,
Archive.org, Wayback, SourceForge, Tiddlyhost and live Wikimedia sites were not
queried. No GitHub Actions relay or third-party proxy was used to evade that
restriction. Useful follow-up queries, **not new evidence**, are:

- GitLab Projects API: search `wiki in a jar`, `morewikiinajar`, `tiddlywiki`,
  record pagination, project id, commit, license and source archive SHA-256.
- Internet Archive advanced search: title/identifier queries for `WikiInAJar`,
  `morewikiinajar`, and `WikiInAJar-0.8-20081128-bin.zip`; inspect item metadata
  and checksums before downloading executables.
- Wayback CDX for `morewikiinajar.sourceforge.net/*`: list captures by timestamp,
  collapse duplicate digests, recover source archives/changelogs and distinguish
  an archived page about a file from the actual file bytes.

Recovering one of those artifacts would justify a separate historical build and
three-way source/bytecode comparison. Until then, the new release names retain
“repository edition” labels and do not claim historical byte identity.

== 10. Validation and remaining acceptance checks ==

Completed local checks (commands in the tool README):

- Targeted catalog/exchange/calendar/TiddlyWiki/Webxdc/DjVu suite: **22 Node tests**;
  **2 Workbench ↔ WebCrypto interoperability tests**. The complete project suite
  also passes; Java/server integration is run separately from its default skip.
- Executable-JAR integration: actual ACME requests from an otherwise empty
  working directory; all three edition redirects; raster/DjVu/WASM handling;
  exact-byte vault digest; path/encoding/symlink rejection; unauthorized, stale,
  missing-precondition, oversized and malformed-UTF-8 saves; concurrent writes;
  restore and restart persistence; protected opaque vault envelopes; read-only mode.
- Two consecutive fixture builds produced identical `SHA256SUMS`.
- Both fixture and full-repository MediaWiki XML validated against the pinned
  0.11 XSD with offline imports; every unique full-snapshot vault blob was read
  back from the JAR and checked for byte length and SHA-256.
- Real headless Chromium: library loads a source page, the calendar shows all 31
  October days, event creation navigates to the dated page, native TiddlyWiki
  boots into **Repository Home**, all source tiddlers and metadata links are
  present, edits survive reload, and the local DjVu sample renders. Full-size
  mobile layouts have no horizontal overflow; busy calendar days use counts
  and a full expandable agenda rather than giant wrapped title columns. No
  page JavaScript errors were observed in the completed smoke run.
- JavaCard grammar: one source parsed by the real JDK parser, zero syntax errors.

Pending acceptance checks are **not** hidden behind passing unit tests: historical
More Wiki source recovery; full Ghidra import/decompilation; JavaCard API/CAP and
hardware simulation; legacy appletviewer execution; messenger/device sync;
actual MediaWiki instance import; live Tiddlyhost API behavior; GitLab/Archive
recovery; AOT/WASM performance and storage benchmarks; public-facing security review.
